title: Phone Confessions
blurb: Camera rolls, group chats and search history. Mild first, spicy for the brave.

truth: How many unread notifications are on your phone right now?
What's the most embarrassing app on your home screen?
What was your first mobile phone, and how much do you miss it?
What's the weirdest thing in your camera roll right now?
What's your screen time average, and does it make you wince?
What's the longest you've gone without checking your phone?
What's the most-played song in your streaming history that you'd rather hide?
What's your most-used emoji, and what does it say about you?
Which contact in your phone has the funniest name saved?
What's the last meme you saved?
Have you ever sent a message to the wrong group chat? What happened?
What's the oddest thing you've ever used your phone's torch for?
What's the cracked screen or phone disaster story you tell the most?
How many photos do you take of the same thing before you pick one?
What's the strangest voicemail you've ever left or received?
What's the worst thing about your phone's autocorrect?
What's your most-liked post ever, and what was it of?
What's the most embarrassing thing you've said to a voice assistant?
What do you do with your phone when you're trying to look busy?
What's the oldest photo you still have on your phone?
What's a notification sound you hate with every fibre of your being?
What's a game on your phone you've spent too much time on?
dare: Show the group your most recent photo of a pet, plant or meal.
Read the last three messages in your family group chat aloud in a movie trailer voice.
Take a selfie with the most ridiculous face you can pull and show it off.
Let the group pick a funny contact name to rename someone in your phone for the night.
Read out your next calendar event in a dramatic news anchor voice.
Let the person on your left set your wallpaper to something silly for an hour.
Do an impression of your own ringtone and make the group guess the song.
Record a 10-second voice memo as a pirate announcing the weather.
Open your music app and play 10 seconds of the most recent song, then commit to the dance.
Show the group your home screen and explain every app as if you're selling the phone.
Draw a portrait of the person opposite with your eyes closed, on your phone, and show everyone.
Send a friend a text containing only a word the group picks, no context.
Use your phone's voice-to-text to dictate a sentence the group gives you, no editing.
Take a photo of the room as if you're a real estate agent and describe it dramatically.
Set an alarm called 'Time to be amazing' for tomorrow morning, and show everyone.
Film a 10-second unboxing of whatever is in your pocket or bag, then show the group.
Hold your phone to your ear and have a one-sided argument with your own voice assistant.
Show the group the most-used row of your emoji keyboard.
Take a photo of your most dramatic 'I just saw a ghost' face and show it off.
Take a panorama photo where the person next to you appears twice, then show it.
Switch your phone to a language you can't read for two minutes.
Read out your next notification in your best movie narrator voice.
Post a story with a harmless caption the group picks, and delete it after the next round.

truth: What's the most embarrassing thing in your search history that you'll admit?

What's the cringiest message you've ever sent to someone you liked?
What's a photo on your phone you'd hate this room to see?
What's the most embarrassing thing you've posted online and later deleted?
What's a message you drafted but never sent?
Who's the most recent person you muted without telling them?
What's the last thing you screenshot to send to a friend about someone else?
What's the most awkward 'like' you've ever accidentally given?
What's the worst thing you've sent that you couldn't unsend?
Which contact do you avoid replying to the longest?
What's something you've typed in a text and then deleted because it was too honest?
dare: Let the group read out your last sent text message.
Show the group your most recent three search suggestions.
Let the group pick a contact for you to send a single funny emoji to, with no explanation.
Read out the funniest message in your phone, if you're okay with it.
Show the room the oldest unanswered message on your phone.
Pick a friend in your contacts and send them a voice message singing happy birthday.
Read out the last message you sent to a crush or partner.
Hand your phone to the person on your left and let them scroll your photos for 10 seconds, with you picking the album.
Let the group write a harmless one-line status about you, and post it for ten minutes.
Read your last three notes or reminders out loud.
Show the group your favourites contact list and explain why each person is there.
Take the worst selfie you can and send it to the group chat.
